title: is_valid_mailbox_host accepts arbitrary public hostnames — outbox can reach public internet
description: is_valid_mailbox_host: if the host portion does not parse as IpAddr, the function returns true unconditionally. The character-set filter ([a-zA-Z0-9.-]) blocks injection but not public hostnames. A peer whose contact record has peer_mailbox_host='evil.example.com' (stored from a Peer/deliver) will cause the outbox to make outbound HTTPS requests to arbitrary public hostnames. The tailnet-only constraint depends on every peer_mailbox_host resolving to a tailnet IP; this function does not enforce that for hostname-form addresses. Fix: require that non-bracketed non-IP hosts end in a known tailnet DNS suffix, OR resolve all hostnames through tailscaled, OR reject hostnames entirely and require IP literals.
